title: Craig Kimbrel exits after vomiting near mound in Royals-Marlins game: ‘He’s very, very sick’
content:
If there is one moment Craig Kimbrel would like to forget from what has otherwise been a Hall of Fame-caliber career, it is the sight of him puking near the mound Thursday night before he left the Kansas City Royals’ series finale against the Miami Marlins.

Kimbrel, pitching for his third big-league club this season, was summoned by Royals manager Matt Quatraro to protect a 4-3 lead in the top of the seventh.

As Kimbrel got set to face Marlins first baseman Kyle Stowers, the right-hander crouched near the mound as liquid spewed from his mouth before the broadcast camera cut away.

“Now we are not going to show you Craig Kimbrel because it is so hot outside, he’s very, very sick on the mound right now,” Marlins play-by-play announcer Kyle Sielaff said on the broadcast. “So we will give him a little bit of privacy here.”

Kimbrel, who has 441 saves in his 17-year career, recorded just two outs before exiting due to nausea, the Royals announced. Kansas City went on to win 7-3.

The game-time temperature at Kauffman Stadium in Kansas City, Mo., was 97 degrees, with humidity hovering around 50 percent.

“Started selling Buicks,” analyst and former major leaguer Jeff Nelson quipped.

Kimbrel is not the only one to be overcome by the heat this season.

On Monday, home-plate umpire Manny Gonzalez exited the game between the Cincinnati Reds and the San Diego Padres with heat exhaustion, needing assistance to leave the field. The 14-minute delay came as temperatures reached 90 degrees with 61 percent humidity in Cincinnati. Earlier this year, Tampa Bay right-hander Jonathan Heasley puked on the mound in his lone appearance of the 2026 campaign. Heasley did finish his outing.

Last season, Elly De La Cruz drew attention after he vomited on the field during the fourth inning of a mid-June game in St. Louis, only to slug a go-ahead, two-run home run three innings later.

“He drank a bunch of water — I mean a bunch,” Reds manager Terry Francona said at the time. “He went right out and got rid of it. Probably could’ve made some money — that’s game-used. It’s probably worth something.”
